deeds.name: Fulfil bounties
deeds.text: the bounties the heroes have brought home

deeds.name: Throw back raids and assaults
deeds.text: the town standing firm against its foes

deeds.name: See menaces ended
deeds.text: a menace gone from the map

deeds.name: Keep the town content
deeds.text: a long stretch of contented folk

feats.name: Inspiring Leader
feats.text: Hold one more Inspiration, and gain one now.

feats.name: Practised Hand
feats.text: On skills you are trained in, a d20 under 6 counts as a 6. No natural 1s.

feats.name: Cool Head
feats.text: A miss within 5 of the DC is a success at a cost, where a choice allows one.

motion.success: The hall comes round to the mayor's view (+1 Mandate).
motion.failure: The hall grumbles, but goes along.

submit.success: The mayor kneels without grovelling, and the town respects it (+3 Mandate).

refuse.success: The answer gives the foe pause; some of its followers slip away.

envoy.success: The mayor's own letter goes down well (+4 standing).

crackdown.success: The mayor faces the crooks down in person (+1 Mandate).

backgrounds.name: Disgraced councillor
backgrounds.text: You sat on a League town's council until a scandal. You know how a chamber turns, and you have advantage on checks in council stories.

backgrounds.name: Soldier
backgrounds.text: You stood in a League levy when the beacons were lit. Fighters listen to you, and you have advantage on checks in war stories.

backgrounds.name: Acolyte
backgrounds.text: You lit the beacon-lamps at a League temple. The faithful trust you, and you have advantage on checks in stories of faith.

backgrounds.name: Sage
backgrounds.text: You copied Caldor's old records for the Unshut Book. Old things speak to you, and you have advantage on checks in stories of the old world.

backgrounds.name: Toll collector
backgrounds.text: You kept the tolls on a League road and missed nothing. You have advantage on checks in the town's own troubles.

backgrounds.name: Caravan guard
backgrounds.text: You rode guard on the Oasis road. You know weather and wild country, and you have advantage on checks in stories from the road.

backgrounds.name: Criminal
backgrounds.text: You learned the trade on the wharves of the Free Ports, and you still know who to ask. You have advantage on checks in stories of the factions.

stages.text: Two caravan hands and a militiaman off duty are trading punches over a game of knucklebones, and half of {tavern} has taken sides.

options.label: Wade in and pull them apart

success.text: You haul the loudest of them out by the collar, and the room cheers.

partial.text: You break it up, but a table and two benches don't survive it.

failure.text: You end up on the floor with ale in your hair. People will tell that one for weeks.

success.text: The room goes quiet at the mayor's voice, and the brawlers sit down sheepishly.

failure.text: Nobody hears you over the noise. The watch clears the room at midnight.

options.label: Buy a round for the house

success.text: Nothing ends a fight like free ale.

ignored.text: The watch drags them out by dawn. Someone's tooth is still under a table.

stages.text: A smiling stranger has won at three-dragon every night this week, and the losers say his deck has more dragons than it should.

success.text: You catch the card in his sleeve. His winnings go back to the town.

failure.text: You see nothing amiss. He tips his hat to you on his way out.

options.label: Read the man, not the cards

success.text: One look tells you he's lying. Faced with it, he pays back the worst of his marks and leaves.

failure.text: He seems an honest sort to you. The losers disagree.

critical.text: You cheat the cheat, and he leaves town with his pockets turned out.

success.text: You beat him at his own game, to roars from the tables.

failure.text: He takes you for a purse of the town's gold, and smiles while he does it.

fumble.text: He takes you for everything you brought, and the whole tavern saw it.

ignored.text: He leaves on the morning cart with a purse full of {town}'s coin.

stages.text: {hero} has bet a crowd at the well that nobody in {town} can out-wrestle them, and the crowd is calling for the mayor.

success.text: You pin {heroName} in the mud to cheers. They laugh and buy you a drink.

partial.text: You last longer than anyone thought, and {heroName} claps you on the back.

failure.text: {heroName} throws you in the trough, then helps you out, grinning.

success.text: Your toast to {town}'s champions has the crowd stamping. {heroName} goes red to the ears.

failure.text: The toast falls flat, and {heroName} wanders off.

success.text: The crowd breaks up. {heroName} sulks, but does as you say.

failure.text: {heroName} laughs in your face and the crowd laughs with them.

ignored.text: Nobody takes the wager. {heroName} grumbles that this town has no sport in it.

stages.text: {hero} has been seen buying rope and rations, and the word at the inn is that they mean to leave for a town that pays better.

options.label: Remind them what the town owes them

success.text: You talk until the candles gutter. {heroName} unpacks.

partial.text: {heroName} stays, for now, and for a little gold.

failure.text: {heroName} hears you out and says nothing. The pack stays by the door.

options.label: Find out what is really wrong

success.text: It isn't the pay. It's that nobody thanked them for the last one. You do.

failure.text: You guess wrong, and {heroName} is offended.

options.label: Send a purse to their room

success.text: Gold talks. {heroName} stays.

ignored.text: Nobody from the hall comes. {heroName} takes it as an answer.

stages.text: The sending stone at the hall cracks with a voice: {party} is pinned by a storm far out in the wilds, and {hero} asks whether to press on or turn back.

options.label: Read the weather and guide them

critical.text: You call every turn of the storm right. {heroName} swears {town} has a weather-witch for a mayor.

success.text: They come through the storm on your word, and {heroName} won't forget it.

failure.text: Your advice takes them into the teeth of it. They come through, but it costs them.

options.label: Find a safe road on the old maps

success.text: An old road of the drovers runs in the lee of the ridge. They find it.

failure.text: The old road is long gone under the scree.

success.text: They sit it out in a cave, and come on when the sky clears.

failure.text: Holding fast means three cold nights with too little food.

ignored.text: The stone stays silent. When they come home, {heroName} asks why nobody answered.

stages.text: {councillor}, the {seat}, has called a fellow councillor a thief in open session, and both refuse to sit until the other apologises.

success.text: A shared jug, a long night and a handshake. The council sits again.

partial.text: They sit again, glaring at each other across the table.

failure.text: Your peace lasts until the first vote.

critical.text: The accounts don't lie: a fat purse was skimmed, and every coin of it comes back.

success.text: There was a thief, and the gold comes back. {councillor} was right, and insufferable about it.

failure.text: You find nothing, and both of them feel accused.

success.text: They go back to work, sullen but quiet.

failure.text: {councillor} walks out of the chamber, and half the town hears why.

ignored.text: The feud festers, and the town's business waits on it.

stages.text: A messenger brings a sealed letter from {faction}: their people will be at the town's service, for a seat at your table and a blind eye now and then.

success.text: You get their help and a gift for the treasury, and give them very little.

failure.text: They think you greedy, and go away to think again.

success.text: You shake on it. Some in town mutter about the company you keep.
The messenger leaves pale, and the town hears that its mayor can't be bought.

failure.text: They laugh at the threat, and remember it.

ignored.text: No answer comes from the hall, and the silence is taken as an insult by {faction}.

stages.text: The watch has caught someone copying the treasury's books by candlelight. Under the ink on their fingers is the mark of {faction}.

success.text: They talk, and the fine for their release is paid in full by {faction}.

failure.text: They say nothing at all, and are gone from the cells by morning.

options.label: Turn them, and feed {faction} false books

critical.text: Every false figure is believed, and {faction} is made a laughing stock.

success.text: The spy goes home with books that lead {faction} nowhere, and the fine is paid twice over.

failure.text: The spy sees through you, and every word of it goes back to {faction}.

options.label: Let them go with a warning

success.text: The courtesy is not lost on {faction}. The town is less pleased.

ignored.text: The spy is sprung from the cells in the night, and the books go with them.

stages.text: A rider under a filthy white rag waits at the ford. {menace} wants to talk about who the valleys belong to.

success.text: You learn more from what the envoy won't say than from what they do, and the heroes hear all of it.

failure.text: The envoy learns more about {town} than you do about them.

success.text: The envoy rides off sure the town has twice the walls it has. {menace} turns its eyes elsewhere a while.

failure.text: The envoy smiles at the lie. {menace} knows now how thin the walls are.

options.label: Send them off with a warning

success.text: The envoy goes white and spurs away. The town watches from the walls, and cheers.

failure.text: The envoy laughs and spits in the ford.

ignored.text: The rider waits a day and goes. Out in the hills, {menace} takes the silence for fear.

stories.title: The host of {menace} is on the road

stages.text: Scouts say the host of {menace} will camp tonight at the ford below {town}. There is still time to do something about it.

options.label: Lead a sally against the camp

critical.text: You fall on the camp in the small hours and burn half its wagons. You're home before dawn, and the bells ring for you.

success.text: You strike the camp at moonset and are back behind the walls by first light. The host will march on lighter.

partial.text: You do real harm to the camp, and bring back wounded.

failure.text: The camp was waiting for you. You get most of your people back.

fumble.text: It goes wrong from the first step. The host jeers at the walls all night.

success.text: You break the old weir at midnight, and the river does the rest. The host must find another crossing.

failure.text: The weir holds against everything you throw at it.

success.text: By morning the camp believes the town has a dragon. Deserters stream off into the hills.

failure.text: Your false rumours never reach the camp's fires.

options.label: Ring the bells and man the walls

success.text: No tricks tonight: every hand to the walls, and the town sleeps a little easier for it.

stages.text: While the host searches for a crossing, a deserter from the ranks of {menace} comes to the gate, offering its order of march for a pardon.

success.text: The deserter is genuine. The heroes know now where the host is weakest.

failure.text: It was a ruse: the false order of march costs the town half a day.

success.text: The host sees what {town} does with its kind.

failure.text: The town is sickened by it.

ignored.text: The deserter slips away in the night.
Nobody stops them. The host camps at the ford and sings all night, and the town listens.

stages.text: Smoke at dawn over the outlying farms. Raiders of {menace} have driven off the cattle, and the farmers want them back.

success.text: You find the cattle in a gully, and the raiders guarding them run.

failure.text: The trail goes cold in the rocks, and an arrow from the heights wounds one of your riders.

success.text: The farmers band together and bring half the herd home themselves.

failure.text: The farmers go home, and the herd is gone.

options.label: Pay the farmers for their loss

success.text: Gold won't bring the cattle back, but the farmers know the hall stands with them.

ignored.text: The farmers count their losses and curse the hall.

stages.text: The lamps of {god} burned blue all night at the shrine, and the townsfolk want to know what it means.

success.text: A sign of favour, you tell them, and the shrine is full by evening.

failure.text: Your reading convinces nobody, the priests least of all.

options.label: Call it a blessing and throw a feast

success.text: The town feasts under blue lamps, and talks of nothing else for days.

failure.text: The feast is a damp affair, and the lamps go out halfway through.

options.label: Say it is only marsh gas

success.text: The sensible folk nod. The priests don't.

failure.text: Marsh gas, in a stone shrine? Nobody believes you.

ignored.text: The lamps burn yellow again by the next night, and the talk turns to the mayor's silence.

stages.text: A peddler has turned up a crown-piece stamped with the sign of {power}. Collectors would pay well for it, and the old folk say such things carry old grudges.

critical.text: It is the real thing, and a rare one. A collector in the south pays a fortune.

success.text: You know the mint and the reign. The town buys it cheap and sells it dear.

failure.text: It's a fake, and the town paid for it.

success.text: An old blessing, not a curse. You give it to the shrine, and sell the peddler's other trinkets.

failure.text: Something cold looks back at you out of the metal. You sleep badly for a week.

success.text: You get it for a song and sell it for a choir.

failure.text: The peddler knows what he has.

ignored.text: The peddler takes the crown-piece south.

stories.title: A child lost in the woods

stages.text: The cooper's daughter went out for mushrooms yesterday and hasn't come home. Her mother is at the hall door.

success.text: You find her by the brook at dusk, cold and cross and quite safe.

failure.text: The search finds nothing. She walks home the next morning, half frozen.

success.text: The old hound has her scent in a moment.

failure.text: The hounds chase a deer for an hour. She's found at dawn.

options.label: Ask a hero to find her

success.text: A hero has her home by supper, on their shoulders.

ignored.text: She finds her own way home after two cold nights, and her mother has things to say about the mayor.

stages.text: A crowd at the granary door is shouting about the price of bread, and someone has brought a torch.

success.text: You stand on a barrel and talk them home, one promise at a time.

partial.text: They go home, with a sack or two of grain each.

failure.text: The granary door gives way. By morning the stores are thinner and tempers no better.

options.label: Buy a wagon of grain from the river barges

success.text: The wagon rolls in at noon, and the crowd cheers it to the granary.
The torch goes out. The crowd goes home, muttering.

failure.text: The crowd boos you off the steps.

ignored.text: The granary is broken into in the night.

stages.text: A drunk at {tavern} is selling a map to {site}, where he swears his grandfather saw lights under the hill.

success.text: The landmarks are real. The town buys the map for the price of his supper.

failure.text: It looks like nonsense to you, and you buy it anyway, out of pity.

success.text: The map is smudged, but the hill is on it.
By the fourth ale he's told you the way for free.

failure.text: He falls asleep halfway through the story.

ignored.text: He sells the map to a passing tinker.

stages.text: Folk without homes have raised a camp of hides and sailcloth by the river. The neighbours want it gone, and the camp wants a roof.

success.text: A few doors open, a few hands are hired, and the camp shrinks by half.

failure.text: Nobody has room to spare, or so they say.

success.text: A building bee by the river, with a fiddler and a cauldron of stew. Two cabins go up by dark.

failure.text: Three people come, and one of them is the fiddler.

success.text: The camp moves on downriver. The neighbours are pleased, and nobody else is.

failure.text: The camp won't move, and the whole town watches you fail to move it.

ignored.text: The camp stays, and so do the complaints.

stages.text: Three households are down with a sweating fever, and a fourth this morning. The herbwife says it came up the river.

success.text: Willow bark, clean water and long nights. The fever breaks in every house.

partial.text: The fever breaks, but the herbs and the nursing cost the town.

failure.text: The fever is beyond your herbs.

success.text: The lanes are closed and kept closed. The fever burns out where it started.

failure.text: People slip through the cordon at night.

success.text: The priests of {god} go house to house, and the fever goes with them.

stages.text: The fever has jumped the lanes. Doors are chalked, and people are blaming strangers.

success.text: A fouled well by the tannery. You seal it, and the fever fades within the week.

failure.text: You never find the source. The fever runs its course, and takes its toll.

success.text: Whether it's {god} or the rest, the town comes through, and remembers who sat with them.

failure.text: The prayers bring comfort, and nothing else.

options.label: Send for a healer at any price

success.text: A healer from the south arrives in a lacquered coach, and earns every coin.

ignored.text: The fever runs through the town and burns itself out.
The fever burns itself out, but not before half the town has had it.
